conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.2 Ground (Fundamental) Tissue System
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.2 Ground (Fundamental) Tissue System

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Casparian strips in the endodermis force water into the symplastic route. The pericycle gives endogenous origin to lateral roots and secondary vascular cambium.

conceptBreakdown.content:
The Ground Tissue System consists of all plant tissues except the epidermal and vascular systems.

### Core Zonation
• **Hypodermis**: Collenchymatous in dicot stems; sclerenchymatous in monocot stems.
• **General Cortex**: Multi-layered parenchymatous storage tissue.
• **Endodermis**: Innermost layer of cortex surrounding the central stele.
  - **Casparian Strips**: Tangential and radial wall thickenings composed of hydrophobic **suberin** and lignin that block apoplastic diffusion and force water through the symplastic selective filter.
  - **Starch Sheath**: Endodermal layer storing abundant starch granules in dicot stems.
• **Pericycle**: Sits between endodermis and vascular bundles. Gives endogenous rise to **lateral roots** and contributes to secondary vascular cambium formation.

conceptBreakdown.content:
Vascular bundles organize primary xylem and phloem elements into conductive strands.

### Primary Bundle Classes
• **Radial**: Xylem and phloem lie on alternate, separate radii separated by non-conductive parenchyma (*Universal diagnostic of ROOTS*).
• **Conjoint Collateral Open**: Xylem and phloem lie on the same radius with an active strip of intrafascicular cambium between them (*Dicot stems*).
• **Conjoint Collateral Closed**: Xylem and phloem lie on the same radius without cambium; enclosed in a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath (*Monocot stems*).
• **Bicollateral**: Phloem and cambium occur on both the outer and inner sides of central xylem ($	ext{Outer Phloem} ightarrow 	ext{Outer Cambium} ightarrow 	ext{Xylem} ightarrow 	ext{Inner Cambium} ightarrow 	ext{Inner Phloem}$; *Cucurbitaceae*, *Solanaceae*).
• **Concentric**:
  - **Amphicribral (Hadrocentric)**: Phloem completely surrounds a central xylem core (*Ferns*).
  - **Amphivasal (Leptocentric)**: Xylem completely surrounds a central phloem core (*Dracaena*, *Yucca*).
